# Parley v0.1.39

Container panes can now complete Codex's browser sign-in. That is the one change
to the app since v0.1.37; v0.1.38 was tagged but never published, because its
only change was to the test suite.

## Codex browser sign-in works inside a container

Codex's browser sign-in finishes by sending your browser to `localhost:1455`.
A container pane runs on Docker's bridge network, so that address on your Mac
never reached the container — the review used to say as much — and the only way
to sign in was the device-code flow.

The container review now has a **Published port** field. Enter `1455` and port
1455 on your Mac is forwarded to port 1455 inside the container, so the sign-in
completes in your browser like it does for a host pane. Leave it empty and
nothing is published: device-code sign-in still works with no port, and every
container you set up before this release behaves exactly as it did.

The review says which route each vendor needs. Codex: 1455 for browser sign-in,
or empty for device code. Claude: its paste-code sign-in needs no port.

### What the forward is, and is not

- It listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Nothing else on your network can reach it.
- It is one port, forwarded to the same number inside the container. Ports
  below 1024 and above 65535 are refused before Docker is asked to do anything.
- Docker's network mode, the mounted folders and the dropped capabilities are
  unchanged. This publishes a port; it does not widen the container.
- If something on your Mac is already listening on that port, Docker refuses to
  start the container and the pane says so.
- Only the container review sets it. An agent cannot request it, including
  through team sessions.

The pane badge shows `CONTAINER · PORT 1455`, and Status Center's container
records say which port a recorded container forwards.

## Also since v0.1.37

The test suite no longer leaves empty files in `~/Library/Preferences` on every
run. It had left 1,626 of them since August. This does not affect the app; it is
recorded here so the version history stays honest.

## Compatibility

Agent protocol is unchanged at 32, and no pane needs restarting. Existing
container configurations decode with no published port and keep working.

Validated: 339 native checks, 53 Node tests, public scan, platform scan and
build. The new check was watched failing before the feature existed, and its
refusal half was proved by removing the range guard and watching it fail again.

Not validated here: an actual Codex sign-in through the forward. The check
proves what Docker is asked to do; completing the sign-in needs a real account,
and it is step 2 of the container scenario in `docs/test-scenarios.md`.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
